cohort: The study included 55 pregnant patients with antiphospholipid syndrome and a control group of 55 healthy pregnant women treated at the Clinic for Ob/Gyn, Clinical Center of Serbia, from 2006 to 2012.
finding: Patients with antiphospholipid syndrome experienced significantly higher rates of premature delivery, pregnancy loss, thrombocytopenia, intrauterine growth restriction, and perinatal asphyxia compared to healthy pregnant women, with the number of previous miscarriages being the most important prognostic factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes.
